titulo: Verbal aspect: Two forms for each verb

aula.objetivo: Understand the difference between imperfective and perfective verbs (I was reading × I read), recognize verb pairs and form the perfective with prefixes.

blocos.titulo: Verbal aspect: why verbs come in pairs
blocos.explicacao: A promise kept: why does almost every Russian verb come in a pair? In earlier lessons and vocabulary lists you noticed that almost all Russian verbs appear as a couple: де́лать / сде́лать (to do), чита́ть / прочита́ть (to read), писа́ть / написа́ть (to write), покупа́ть / купи́ть (to buy). The time has come to master this Russian superpower: verbal aspect (Вид глаго́ла). English has a dozen verb tenses ("I read", "I was reading", "I have read", "I had read"...). Russian has only three tenses (past, present and future), but it looks at any action through two different lenses. • 1. Imperfective (НСВ — Несоверше́нный вид) = THE FILM (process, routine, duration). It focuses on the action happening, repeating every day or lasting for a while, whether or not it finished. It corresponds to our "I was reading / I used to read / I read every day". • 2. Perfective (СВ — Соверше́нный вид) = THE PHOTOGRAPH (a single, completed result). It focuses on the end point, the mission accomplished, the finished result of one single occasion. It corresponds to our "I read the whole book / I have written the letter / I bought the ticket". The Compass: imperfective (НСВ) versus perfective (СВ). The big trick of the simple future (perfective): the perfective verb (сде́лать, прочита́ть, написа́ть, купи́ть) has no present. So when you apply the present-tense scissors to it, the result means COMPLETED FUTURE (and it never uses бу́ду!). де́лать (НСВ): я де́лаю (I do / am doing now) · я бу́ду де́лать (I will be doing / working on it). сде́лать (СВ): я сде́лаю (I will do it / I will get it done!) · ты сде́лаешь · он сде́лает.

linhas.1. IMPERFECT́IVO (НСВ) — O F́ILME (ЧИТА́: Process / Duration (for 2 hours, all day) Repetition / Habit (always, every day, often) The general fact (“Have you ever read Tolstoy?”)
linhas.2. PERFECT́IVO (СВ)́ — A FOTOGRAFIA (ПРО: Completed result (“Done, I finished!”) Single, punctual action (once, suddenly) Sequence of events (“I woke up, had coffee and left”)

linhas.1. IMPERFECT́IVO (НСВ) — O F́ILME (ЧИТА́: всегда́ (always) · ча́сто (often) · обы́чно (usually) · ка́ждый день (every day) · до́лго (for a long time) · весь день (all day long)
linhas.2. PERFECT́IVO (СВ)́ — A FOTOGRAFIA (ПРО: уже́ (already) · наконе́ц (finally) · вдруг (suddenly) · сра́зу (immediately) · весь / всю / всё (all, whole)
IT DOES NOT EXIST! (Nobody finishes something in the middle of “right now”!)

linhas.1. IMPERFECT́IVO (НСВ) — O F́ILME (ЧИТА́: Вчера́ я чита́л кни́гу два часа́. (Yesterday I spent two hours reading the book — process.)
linhas.2. PERFECT́IVO (СВ)́ — A FOTOGRAFIA (ПРО: Вчера́ я прочита́л всю кни́гу! (Yesterday I read the whole book — completed!)

linhas.1. IMPERFECT́IVO (НСВ) — O F́ILME (ЧИТА́: Compound future (бу́ду + inf. НСВ, the imperfective): За́втра я бу́ду чита́ть. (I will read / I will be reading.)
linhas.2. PERFECT́IVO (СВ)́ — A FOTOGRAFIA (ПРО: Simple future (conjugate the СВ, perfective, verb!): За́втра я прочита́ю э́ту статью́! (I will read it to the end!)

blocos.explicacao: In Russian, almost every verb has TWO infinitives, called aspects. The imperfective looks at the action as a process, habit or repetition: «Я читал книгу» = I was reading a book (perhaps without finishing it). The perfective looks at the action as a whole, completed, with a result: «Я прочитал книгу» = I read the book to the end. English shows the same idea in the difference between "I was reading" and "I read it through" / "I finished reading". Guiding question: does the process or habit matter (imperfective), or the completed result (perfective)? The perfective is conjugated like any verb (1st or 2nd conjugation) and is often formed with a PREFIX: делать → сделать. Attention: the perfective has no present tense; its present-looking forms mean the future (next lesson). So when you study a verb, always study the pair: imperfective / perfective.
blocos.comparacao: English uses different tenses or extra words for the same verb ("was reading" versus "read through"). Russian uses two different verbs, almost always similar to each other.

exemplos.pt: Yesterday I was reading a book.
Yesterday I read the book (to the end).
Every day I used to read (habit).

erros.motivo: Habit and repetition call for the imperfective.

blocos.enunciado: Say two sentences for each pair: «Я читал книгу. Я прочитал книгу.» «Я писал письмо. Я написал письмо.»
Write the past tense of 5 verbs, in the masculine and the feminine.
